title: Jump Game
prompt:
`nums[i]` is your maximum jump length from index `i`. Starting at index 0, return whether you can reach the last index.

**Example**: `[2,3,1,1,4]` → `true`; `[3,2,1,0,4]` → `false` (every path lands on the 0 at index 3).

**Constraints**: `1 ≤ nums.length ≤ 10^4`, `0 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10^5`.
hints: Do the exact jumps matter, or only how far you could possibly get?
Scan left to right, keeping `reach`, the farthest index reachable from any index you can actually stand on.
`if (i > reach) return false; reach = Math.max(reach, i + nums[i]);`

solution.explanation: Every index ≤ reach can be reached (you can always jump short), so only the frontier matters. If the scan index passes it, there is a gap nobody can jump over. Otherwise the last index was within reach. O(n) time, O(1) space.
